metadata.case_name: FU CHUEN SING v. RYAN (HK) LTD

plaintiff.occupation_before: distributor on overnight shift (delivery worker of newspapers and magazines)
plaintiff.occupation_after: salesman for a cable TV company (from 1 September 2008); later salesman for another cable TV company (from 28 October 2009)

injuries.description: Back sprain / Back injury resulting in persistent back pain
source: he sprained his back (“chok”) when he was trying to stop the sudden falling of papers.
Employees’ Compensation (Ordinary Assessment) Board assessed that the Plaintiff suffered “Back injury resulting in persistent back pain” and loss of earning capacity of 0.5%.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

manifestations.description: range of movement of lumbosacral spine was full but mildly limited by pain
low back pain and tenderness at the paraspinal muscles on the left side of lumbar spine
forward flexion of the back was to knee level
extension of the back was limited
back pain when walking up and down stairs
right shoulder and neck pain, right arm cramp
unable to bend his back below 90 degrees
unable to stand for more than 1-2 hours
unable to sit for more than 30 minutes
sexual activity affected by back pain
unable to participate in sports activities such as playing basketball, swimming and running

treatments_received: physiotherapy (28 sessions at Physiotherapy Department of TMH including shortwave diathermy, mobilization and strengthening exercises and condition training)
occupational therapy (1 work assessment session and 2 sessions and discharged with home program and stretching exercise taught)
out-patient follow-up sessions (5 sessions at YFSHC, 46 sessions at YLJCHC, 2 sessions at TMC, 1 session at TMH and 1 session at POH)

losses.description: Back pain when walking up and down stairs; unable to stand for more than 1-2 hours; unable to sit for more than 30 minutes; unable to bend his back below 90 degrees

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Unable to participate in sports activities such as playing basketball, swimming and running

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: Sexual activity affected by back pain
